pr_title: util/ranger: extract multi-column DNF conditions as access conditions
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/18118

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/14795 can be closed as well.

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

- In ranger, for composite indexes, after we extract prefix column equal / in conditions, call ranger recursively for the remained expressions.
- For CNF filters, if we cannot extract prefix column equal / in conditions directly, call ranger recursively for each CNF item to detect column equal / in conditions in more complicated forms.
- For CNF filters like `(a,b) in ((1,1),(2,2)) and c > 0 and a in (1,2)`, compare DNF equal conditions extracted with direct equal conditions extracted, and choose the one covers more columns as prefix column conditions. i.e, `(a,b) in ((1,1),(2,2))` instead of `a in (1,2)` in this case.

How it Works:

Compared with the previous implementation, which calls `detachColumnCNFConditions` for the remained expressions directly, the new approach is more general and reasonable, and it can handle more complicated cases than before.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

issue_context.title: can not use point get plan for a DNF condition
comments: For this case, we'd better have a rule to formalize the expressions instead of doing it when converting to filter to range.

review_comments: Is there a situation where &DetachRangeResult{} is returned to the caller and causes an error? Because usually the caller will only check whether it is nil.

Conventionally, when we return an empty `DetachRangeResult`, it means that the filter is constantly false, for example, https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/util/ranger/detacher.go#L187, so if we always follow this convention, IMHO there should be no problem?

For example, https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/5153a4155a9ac1ad6c7266e00239819e8dc1ba13/planner/core/rule_max_min_eliminate.go#L81 may receive empty `DetachRangeResult` by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/5153a4155a9ac1ad6c7266e00239819e8dc1ba13/util/ranger/detacher.go#L371, but it doesn't check and use the return value directly.

Hmmm, the example you give has no problem since `result.EqCondCount` is 0? I get your concerns, it is true that returning an empty `DetachRangerResult` is not that graceful, we can refactor this later in another PR, like say introducing a new field into `DetachRangerResult` to indicate those constantly false filters. Since there already exists codes returning empty `DetachRangerResult`, and the refactor is not related to the problem this PR aims to solve, I prefer not to do it in this PR.
OK. This sounds great. I have no other questions.
